claim: External repo affaan-m/ECC: 'no compromise found' stated as the verdict after targeted pattern scans of install scripts, hooks and part of the code.
correction: Owner: the scan did not read the other ~4700 files, so the verdict was a scope overreach. Full read of 1629 instruction files and 726 code files followed; final wording became 'no malware, exfiltration or injection found in what was read', with the unread parts listed.

claim: Uncommitted working-copy changes: ~1600 files called unique ('nowhere on GitHub') after comparing them with origin/main only.
correction: Owner: they may exist in other branches. Content hashes checked against objects of all 262 remote branches incl. history: 369 more files were already on GitHub. Only those 538 on-GitHub files were removed; 1223 kept.

claim: Critical_Review_Protocol_V1 draft: 'a shift of corrections from owner to self/challenger in the ledger shows the checks are working'.
correction: Independent challengers (Codex/GPT and Gemini via Antigravity, read-only) showed the ledger counts only noticed corrections with no denominator, so it cannot prove effectiveness. Protocol now marks effectiveness UNVERIFIED until a seeded benchmark with baseline runs; also added tiers, a universal-claim confidence cap and three error classes they identified.
evidence_ref: PR claude/critical-review, challenge transcripts summarised in the PR

claim: Route coverage: '8 files are routed by two domains' and 'about 4200 notes lack a route', from a static re-implementation of the routing rules run on a GitHub clone.
correction: Running the real router (build_route_manifest.py --json) gave 0 files with more than one route and 4230 unrouted, of which only 151 are real gaps (108 nested SKILL.md, 25 Casa3D docs, 13 .claude files, 5 root entry files); the rest are support files or by-design exclusions. The static script was a proxy for the router, not the router.

claim: Widening the skills domain root from .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md to .agents/skills/**/SKILL.md only closes a coverage gap (108 nested SKILL.md get a route) and changes no access.
correction: The skills domain is PUBLIC with default trust verified and is the one domain cloud_web.export publishes, so the widening would have exported 108 unreviewed, mostly imported nested SKILL.md files (one a template) as verified. Nested files moved to a separate skills_nested domain (INTERNAL, unverified, templates excluded); skills root reverted; a test pins that the export cannot read any added domain.

claim: All of 20_TESTS/** can stay without a route because it only holds tests and fixtures.
correction: 20_TESTS/README.md and OUTCOME_CLI_TEST_PLAN.md are documentation, not fixtures; they now have a tests_docs route and the unrouted glob is narrowed to 20_TESTS/fixtures/** plus one marker file.

claim: Gap 3: the vault lacks a layered table of contents generated from vault_domains.yaml and needs one built.
correction: vault_list("*") (MCP and CLI) already lists the domains live from vault_domains.yaml, which is the top layer; AGENTS.md:116 and CLAUDE.md:24 point agents to it. A committed TOC would duplicate it and go stale. Gap 3 reduced to the navigation-link check (32 hits: 14 dead paths fixed, 2 false positives (gitignored folder) removed by the checker, 16 deliberate mentions of retired roots listed with reasons).

claim: Gap 2: CLAUDE.md is bloated (8,984 tokens per request) and duplicates AGENTS.md; make AGENTS.md canonical and CLAUDE.md a thin pointer to save tokens.
correction: The 8,984 figure was measured on 2026-10-21 when CLAUDE.md had 23,104 chars; it now has 13,479 (about 5.3k tokens at the measured 1.56 ratio). Only 10 of 135 longer CLAUDE.md sentences nearly repeat AGENTS.md. The same measurement shows Claude Code does not load AGENTS.md while CLAUDE.md exists, so a pointer saves nothing unless it imports AGENTS.md (about 5.7k tokens). The remaining issue is rules Claude only reaches through a pointer, not size.
